topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and introduces the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen and damage recognition by pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system senses microbial products and cellular damage through pattern recognition receptors, their intracellular signaling cascades, and the inflammasome.

topics.label: Cellular responses, leukocyte trafficking, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how mediator release by sentinel cells directs leukocyte extravasation into tissues, lymphatic drainage, and the systemic consequences of severe inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inflammatory responses are shut down, how tissues undergo healing and remodeling, and why chronic inflammation or granuloma formation can arise.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the complement system.
